title: Definition
body_md:
A dg $\mathbb N$-modules amounts to the data of a functor 
    \[
    X: \mathbb N \longrightarrow \mathsf{dg}~\Bbbk\text{-}\mathsf{mod}.
    \]    
    The object $X(n)$ is called the arity $n$ part of $X$. We denote $\mathsf{dg}~\mathbb N\text{-}\mathsf{mod}$
    the category of dg $\mathbb N$-modules.
head: environment
name: dg $\mathbb N$-modules

title: Definition
body_md: A \textit{planar dg operad} $\mathcal{P}$ amounts to the data of a monoid $(\mathcal{P},\gamma,\eta)$ in the category of dg $\mathbb N$-modules with respect to the composition product.
head: environment
name: Planar dg operad

title: Definition
body_md: An augmented planar dg operad $\mathcal{P}$ amounts to the data of a planar dg operad $(\mathcal{P},\gamma,\eta)$ equipped with a morphism of planar dg operads $\nu: \mathcal{P} \longrightarrow \mathcal{I}$ such that $\nu \circ \eta = \mathrm{id}.$
head: environment
name: Augmented planar dg operad

title: Definition
body_md: A \textit{planar dg cooperad} $\mathcal{C}$ amounts to the data of a comonoid $(\mathcal{C}, \Delta, \epsilon)$ in the category of dg $\mathbb N$-modules with respect to the composition product.
head: environment
name: Planar dg cooperad

title: Definition
body_md: A coaugmented planar dg cooperad $\mathcal{C}$ amounts to the data of a planar dg cooperad $(\mathcal{C}, \Delta, \epsilon)$ equipped with a morphism of planar dg cooperads $\mu: \mathcal{I} \longrightarrow \mathcal{C}$ such that $\epsilon \circ \mu = \mathrm{id}$.
head: environment
name: Coaugmented planar dg cooperad

title: \sc Remark
body_md: One can combine these notations. For instance the $n$-levelled reduced planar tree endofunctor $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n}(X)$ is obtained by taking the sum over non trivial trees whose height is at most $n$.
head: environment

title: \sc Remark
body_md:
Notice that, for all $n \geq 0$, there is a canonical isomorphism
\[
\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1} X \cong \mathcal{I} \oplus X \circ_\mathrm{pl} \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n} X.
\]
that yields an isomorphism $\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} X \cong \mathcal{I} \oplus X \circ \mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pl}} X$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
The planar tree module endofunctor $\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}$ admits the following monad structure:

\medskip

\begin{enumerate}
\item The unit $\eta_X: X \longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} X$ is the canonical inclusion, where elements in $X(m)$ are seen as $m$-corollas.

\medskip

\item The product $\gamma_X: \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}~\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (X)$ is given, for a planar tree $t$ with $n$ leaves, as follows
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=0.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
    t(\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} X)(n) \coloneqq (\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} X)(n_1) \otimes \cdots \otimes (\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} X)(n_k)
    \ar[d,"\cong"] \\
	\displaystyle \bigoplus_{t_1, \ldots, t_k} t_1(X)(n_1) \otimes \cdots \otimes t_k(X)(n_k)
	\ar[d] \\
	\displaystyle \bigoplus_{t_1, \ldots, t_k} \mathrm{graft}_t(t_1, \ldots, t_k)(X)(n)~,
\end{tikzcd}
\]
where $\mathrm{graft}_t(t_1, \ldots, t_k)$ is the planar tree obtained from $t$ by replacing each node $i$ by the planar tree $t_i$ which labelled it.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: The category of algebras over the monad $\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}$ is canonically isomorphic to the category of planar dg operads.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The restriction of the structural map to $\mathbb{T}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq 2}$ gives the composition product, and induces an operad structure. Any operad structure can be extended to a full algebra structure over $\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}$ by induction on the level of planar trees.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
The reduced planar tree module endofunctor $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$ admits the following comonad structure:

\medskip

\begin{enumerate}
\item The counit map $\epsilon_X: \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \longrightarrow X$ is the projection onto corollas labelled by $X$. 

\medskip

\item The coproduct $\Delta_X: \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \longrightarrow  \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} ~\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)$ is given by partitioning non-trivial planar trees into non-trivial planar sub-trees. For a planar tree $t$ with $n$ leaves, the coproduct is given by the finite sum over partitions $t_1, \ldots, t_m$ of $t$ into non trivial sub-trees of the maps
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=0.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
    t(X)(n)
    \ar[d, "\cong"]
    \\ t_1(X)(n_1) \otimes \cdots \otimes t_m(X)(n_m)
    \ar[d]
    \\ \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)(n_1) \otimes \cdots \otimes \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)(n_m)
    \ar[d, "\cong"]
    \\  t/(t_1, \ldots, t_m)(\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X))
    \ar[d, hookrightarrow]
    \\\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)~.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This follows from a straightforward checking.
head: environment

label: corollarydecompositionplanarccooperad
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{corollarydecompositionplanarccooperad}
For every natural integer $n \geq 1$, the comonad structure on $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$ restricts to $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n}$ and $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}^{(\leq n)}$, making the natural inclusions 
\[
\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n} \rightarrowtail \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}~, \quad \quad \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}^{(\leq n)} \rightarrowtail \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}~,
\]
morphisms of comonads.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This follows from the definition of the coproduct of the comonad. For every non-trivial tree $t$ with at most $n$-nodes (resp. of height at most $n$) and every partition $t_1, \ldots, t_m$ of $t$, all the planar trees $t_1, \ldots, t_m, t/(t_1, \ldots, t_m)$ have at most $n$-nodes (resp. have height at most $n$).
head: environment

label: lemma: T-cog implique comonoide pour le circ
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemma: T-cog implique comonoide pour le circ}
For every dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebra $(W,\delta_W)$, the following square
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        W
        \ar[r,"\delta_W"] \ar[d,"\delta_W",swap]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W
        \ar[r, two heads]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq 2} W
        \ar[r, "\cong"]
        & W \circ (\mathcal{I} \oplus W)
        \ar[d,rightarrowtail]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W
        &&&  W \circ {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W.
        \ar[lll, "\cong",swap]
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
is a commutative diagram.
head: environment
labels: lemma: T-cog implique comonoide pour le circ

title: Proof
body_md:
This square decomposes into the diagram
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2pc,row sep=2pc]
        W
        \ar[r, "\delta_W"] \ar[d, "\delta_W"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W
        \ar[r, two heads]\ar[d, "\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\delta_W)"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq 2} W
        \ar[r, "\cong"] \ar[d, "\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq 2}(\delta_W)"]
        & W \circ_\mathrm{pl} (W \oplus \mathcal{I})
        \ar[d, "\delta_W \circ_\mathrm{pl} \delta_W"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W
        \ar[r, "\delta_W"]
        &\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W
        \ar[r, two heads]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq 2} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W
        \ar[r, "\cong"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W \circ_\mathrm{pl}  (\mathcal{I} \oplus \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}})
        \ar[d, "\cong"]
        \\ 
        &&& \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W \circ_\mathrm{pl}  {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W
        \ar[d, two heads]
        \\ 
        &&&  W \circ_\mathrm{pl}  {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} W~,
        \ar[uulll, "\cong"]
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$
    of which all the cells are commutative.

label: propositionplanarccooperadff
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This functor is faithful since its composition with the forgetful functor towards dg $\mathbb N$-modules is faithful.
    Let us prove that it is is full.
    Let $(V,\delta_V)$ and $(W,\delta_W)$ be two dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebras
    and let us consider a morphism of coaugmented planar dg cooperads
    $f: \mathcal{I} \oplus V \to \mathcal{I} \oplus W$. Proving that
    $f$ stems from a morphism of dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebras amounts to prove that the restricted map $\overline{f}: V \to W$ is a morphism of dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebras.
    
    \medskip
    
    Since the natural map $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} X
    \to \lim_{n \in \omega^\mathrm{op}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n} X$ is a monomorphism, it suffices to prove that for every natural integer $n \geq 1$
    the diagram
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        V
        \ar[r, "\overline{f}"] \ar[d,"\delta_V",swap]
        & W \ar[d,"\delta_W"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} V
        \ar[d,two heads]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} W
        \ar[d, two heads]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n} V
        \ar[r, "\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n}(\overline{f})"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n} W
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$
    is commutative. 
    
    \medskip
    
    For $n=1$, this square is clearly commutative. Let us assume that it is commutative for an integer $n \geq 1$ and let us prove that is is commutative for $n+1$. The square above for $n+1$ rewrites as the external square of the diagram
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        V
        \ar[r] \ar[d]
        & W
        \ar[d]
        \\
        V \circ_\mathrm{pl} (I \oplus V)
        \ar[r] \ar[d]
        & W \circ_\mathrm{pl} (I \oplus W)
        \ar[d]
        \\
        V \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n} V
        \ar[r] \ar[d, "\cong"']
        & W \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n} W
        \ar[d, "\cong"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n+1} V
        \ar[r]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl},\leq n+1} W~,
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$
    of which all cells are commutative. So we have proven by induction that such a square is commutative for every natural integer $n \geq 1$. Therefore $\overline{f}$ is a morphism of dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebras.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a coaugmented planar dg cooperad. It is \textit{conilpotent} if it belongs to the essential image of the functor $\mathrm{Conil}$ from dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebras to planar dg cooperads. We denote $\mathsf{dg}~\mathsf{Cooperads}^{\mathsf{conil}}_\mathrm{pl}$ the full sub-category of coaugmented planar dg cooperads spanned by conilpotent ones.
head: environment
name: Conilpotent planar dg cooperad

title: \sc Remark
body_md:
The idea behind this definition is the following: a cooperad can also be described in terms of partial decomposition maps
\[
\Delta_i: \mathcal{C}(n+k-1) \longrightarrow \mathcal{C}(n) \otimes \mathcal{C}(k)~,
\]
and it is conilpotent if and only if any iteration of these partial decompositions is eventually trivial. If this is the case, then the data of all the possible iterations is exactly encoded by the $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebra structure.
head: environment

label: proppresentabilityofplanarconilp
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{proppresentabilityofplanarconilp}
    Let $n$ be a natural integer. The forgetful functor 
    \[
    \mathsf{dg}~\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}^{(\leq n)}\text{-}\mathsf{cog} \longrightarrow \mathsf{dg}~\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}\text{-}\mathsf{cog}~.
    \]
    is fully faithful. Furthermore, both categories are presentable, and therefore it admits a right adjoint denoted by $\overline{\mathrm{F}}_n$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The two categories are presentable. It follows from the fact that they are categories of coalgebras over accessible comonads on a presentable category. We refer to \cite{ChingRiehl} for more details. The fact that the functor is fully faithful follows from the fact that the morphism of comonads $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}^{(\leq n)} \longrightarrow \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}$ is object-wise a monomorphism. The fact that it has a right adjoint is a direct consequence of the adjoint lifting theorem, see \cite[Appendix A]{premierpapier}.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a conilpotent planar dg cooperad. Its $n$-\textit{coradical filtration} is given by the conilpotent planar dg cooperad $\mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_n \mathcal{C}$. It induces a ladder diagram 
\[
\mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_0 \mathcal{C} \rightarrowtail \mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_1 \mathcal{C} \rightarrowtail \cdots \mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_n \mathcal{C} \rightarrowtail \cdots~,
\]
indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, where all the arrows are monomorphisms.
head: environment
name: Coradical filtration

title: Proposition
body_md:
Let $n \geq 0$ and $\mathcal{C}$ be a conilpotent planar dg cooperad. Then $\mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_n \mathcal{C}$ fits in the following pullback 
\[
        \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
           \mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_n \mathcal{C} \arrow[dr, phantom, "\lrcorner", very near start]
            \ar[r] \ar[d]
            & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}^{(\leq n)} \mathcal{C}
            \ar[d,rightarrowtail]
            \\
            \mathcal{C}
            \ar[r,"\delta_\mathcal{C}"]
            & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}} \mathcal{C}.
        \end{tikzcd}
\]
in the category of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules, where $\delta_\mathcal{C}$ denotes the dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}$-coalgebra structure of $\mathcal{C}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This directly follows from the results in \cite[Appendix A]{premierpapier}.
head: environment

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $\mathbb S$ be the groupoid whose objects are natural integers and whose morphisms are given by 
    $$
    \hom_{\mathbb S}(n,m) = 
    \begin{cases}
        \emptyset \text{ if }n \neq m~,
        \\
        \mathbb S_n \text{ if }n = m~.
    \end{cases}
    $$
    A \textit{dg} $\mathbb S$\textit{-module} $M$ amounts to the data of a functor 
   	\[
   	M: \mathbb S^\mathrm{op} \longrightarrow \mathsf{dg}~\Bbbk\text{-}\mathsf{mod}
   	\]
    from $\mathbb S^\mathrm{op}$ to dg modules. We denote by $\mathsf{dg}~\mathbb{S}\text{-}\mathsf{mod}$ the category of dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules.
head: environment
name: dg $\mathbb S$-module

title: Lemma
body_md:
The underlying $\mathbb N$-module of $u\mathcal{A} ss$ has the structure of a planar operad.

\begin{enumerate}
\item The unit is given by the identity map of $\Bbbk$.

\medskip

\item The composition is defined as follows. For every $(\sigma, \sigma_1, \ldots, \sigma_k) \in \mathbb S_k \times \mathbb S_{n_1} \times \cdots \times \mathbb S_{n_k}$ the composition of $\sigma \otimes \sigma_1 \otimes  \cdots \otimes  \sigma_k$ is given by the permutation 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=6pc,row sep=2pc]
    \{1, \ldots, n\}
    \ar[d, "\cong"]
    \\
    \{1, \ldots, n_1\} \sqcup \cdots \sqcup \{1, \ldots, n_k\}
    \ar[d, "\sigma_1 \sqcup \cdots \sqcup \sigma_k"]
    \\
    \{1, \ldots, n_1\} \sqcup \cdots \sqcup \{1, \ldots, n_k\}
    \ar[d, "\sigma"]
    \\
    \{1, \ldots, n_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}\} \sqcup \cdots \sqcup \{1, \ldots, n_{\sigma^{-1}(k)}\}
    \ar[d, "\cong"]
    \\
    \{1, \ldots, n\}.
\end{tikzcd}
\]

in $u\mathcal{A} ss (n)$, where $n = n_1 + \cdots + n_k$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This follows from a straightforward check.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md:
The endofunctor $-\otimes \mathbb S$ of the category of dg $\mathbb N$-modules has a canonical structure of lax monoidal functor with respect to the planar composition product $\circ_{\mathrm{pl}}$. 

\begin{enumerate}
\item There is a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal{I} \cong \mathcal{I} \otimes \mathbb S$ given by the identity map,

\medskip

\item and a binatural map of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules
\[
\varphi_{X,Y}: (X  \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y  \otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S
\]
given by
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=6pc,row sep=2pc]
    (X(k) \otimes \{\sigma\}) \otimes 
\left( 
(Y(n_1) \otimes \{\sigma_1\})
\otimes \cdots \otimes
(Y(n_k) \otimes \mathbb \{\sigma_k\})
\right)
\ar[d, "\cong"]
\\
X(k) \otimes 
\left( 
Y(n_1) 
\otimes \cdots \otimes
Y(n_k)
\right)
\ar[d, "\mathrm{Id} \otimes \sigma"]
\\
X(k) \otimes 
\left( 
Y(n_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}) 
\otimes \cdots \otimes
Y(n_{\sigma^{-1}(k)}) 
\right)
\ar[d, "\cong"]
\\
X(k) \otimes 
\left( 
Y(n_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}) 
\otimes \cdots \otimes
Y(n_{\sigma^{-1}(k)}) 
\right)
\otimes \{\lambda\}
\end{tikzcd}
\]
where $\lambda$ is the composition in $u\mathcal{A} ss$ of $\sigma_k \otimes (\sigma_{n_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes \sigma_{n_k})$.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This amounts to showing that the following diagrams
$$
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
    (X  \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y  \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Z  
    \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[r, "\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl} \varphi_{Y,Z}"] \ar[d,"\varphi_{X,Y} \circ_\mathrm{pl} \mathrm{Id}",swap]
    & (X  \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ((Y \circ_\mathrm{pl} Z)  \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[d,"\varphi_{X,Y \circ_\mathrm{pl} Z}"]
    \\
    ((X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y)  \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Z  \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[r,"\varphi_{X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y,Z}"]
    & (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y \circ_\mathrm{pl} Z)  \otimes \mathbb S~,
\end{tikzcd}
$$
and
$$
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
    (X  \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (\mathcal{I}  \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[r,"\varphi_{X,\mathcal{I}}"] \ar[d]
    & (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} \mathcal{I})  \otimes \mathbb S
    \ar[d]
    \\
    X \otimes \mathbb S
    \ar[r, "\cong"]
    & X \otimes \mathbb S
    \\
    (\mathcal{I}  \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (X \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[r,"\varphi_{\mathcal{I},X}"] \ar[u]
    & (\mathcal{I} \circ_\mathrm{pl} X)  \otimes \mathbb S
    \ar[u]
\end{tikzcd}
$$
are commutative for every dg $\mathbb N$-modules $X,Y,Z$. This follows from the associativity and the unitality of the compositions in the planar operad $u\mathcal{A} ss$.
head: environment

label: lemmalaxmonoidalnt
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemmalaxmonoidalnt}
There are natural transformations
\[
\eta: \mathrm{Id}_{\mathbb{N}} \longrightarrow - \otimes \mathbb S
\]

and 
\[
\mu: - \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S \longrightarrow - \otimes \mathbb S
\]

of endofunctors in the category of dg $\mathbb N$-modules, induced, respectively, by the units and the multiplications in the group algebras $\Bbbk[\mathbb{S}_n]$ for all $n \geq 0$. Furthermore, these natural transformations are monoidal natural transformations between lax monoidal functors.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The behaviour of the monad $- \otimes \mathbb S$ with respect to the unit $\mathcal{I}$ is straightforward to check. We check that the two following diagrams 
\[
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3pc,row sep=3.5pc]
        (X \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
        \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\varphi_{X \otimes \mathbb S,Y \otimes \mathbb S}"] \ar[d,"\mu_X \circ_\mathrm{pl} \mu_Y",swap]
        & ((X \otimes \mathbb S )
        \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y \otimes \mathbb S )) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\varphi_{X,Y} \otimes \mathbb S"]
        & (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[d,"\mu_{X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y}"]
        \\
        (X \otimes \mathbb S )
        \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y \otimes \mathbb S )
        \ar[rr,"\varphi_{X,Y}"]
        && 
        (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S
    \end{tikzcd}
\]
and 
\[
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        (X \otimes \mathbb S ) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y \otimes \mathbb S )
        \ar[r,"\varphi_{X,Y}"]
        & (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S \\
        X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y \arrow[u,"\eta_X \circ_\mathrm{pl} \eta_Y"] \arrow[ru,"\eta_{X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y}",swap]~,
        	&
    \end{tikzcd}
\]
are commutative for all dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules $X$ and $Y$. It follows from the compatibility of the compositions in the planar operad $u\mathcal{A} ss$ with the actions of the symmetric groups.
head: environment

title: \sc Remark
body_md:
There is a natural transformation 
\[
\pi: \mathrm{U}(-) \otimes \mathbb S \longrightarrow \mathrm{Id}_{\mathbb{S}}~,
\]
where $\mathrm{U}$ is the forgetful functor from dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules to dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules. For $M$ a dg $\mathbb S$-modules, $\pi_M: \mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb{S} \longrightarrow M$ is given by the dg $\mathbb{S}$-module structure of $M$.

label: lemmacompositioniso
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{lemmacompositioniso}
For every two dg $\mathbb N$-modules $X,Y$, the natural map 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3.5pc,row sep=4pc]
\psi_{X,Y}: (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S \arrow[r,"(\eta_X \circ_\mathrm{pl} \eta_Y) \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
&(X \otimes \mathbb S \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y \otimes \mathbb S) \otimes \mathbb S \arrow[r,"\rho_{X \otimes \mathbb S ,Y \otimes \mathbb S}"]
&(X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is an isomorphism of dg $\mathbb S$-modules.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let us consider the composite map  
    \[
    \mu_{X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y}~(\varphi_{X,Y} \otimes \mathbb S): ((X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y\otimes \mathbb S)) \otimes \mathbb S
    \longrightarrow (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S
    \longrightarrow (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S~.
    \]
    Using Lemma \ref{lemmalaxmonoidalnt} in a straightforward way, one can prove that it factors through $(X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)$ and that the composite map
    \[
    \mu_{X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y}~(\varphi_{X,Y} \otimes \mathbb S)~\psi_{X,Y}: (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S
    \longrightarrow (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)
    \longrightarrow (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S
    \]
    is the identity. To prove that the composite map
    \[
    \psi_{X,Y}~\mu_{X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y}~(\varphi_{X,Y} \otimes \mathbb S):(X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)
    \longrightarrow (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S
    \longrightarrow (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)
    \]
    is the identity, it is enough to prove that the composition
    \[
    ((X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y\otimes \mathbb S)) \otimes \mathbb S
    \longrightarrow
    (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)
    \longrightarrow (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y) \otimes \mathbb S
    \longrightarrow (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)
    \]
    given by $\psi_{X,Y}~\mu_{X \circ_\mathrm{pl} Y}~(\varphi_{X,Y} \otimes \mathbb S)~\rho_{X \otimes \mathbb S ,Y \otimes \mathbb S}$ 
    is equal to the canonical quotient map $\rho_{X \otimes \mathbb S ,Y \otimes \mathbb S}$. Using 
    Lemma \ref{lemmalaxmonoidalnt} again, we can rewrite this composition as:
   	\[
   	\begin{tikzcd}
   	((X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y\otimes \mathbb S)) \otimes \mathbb S \arrow[d,"(\eta_{X \otimes \mathbb S} \circ_\mathrm{pl} \eta_{Y \otimes \mathbb S}) \otimes \mathbb{S}"] \\
   	((X \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y\otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)) \otimes \mathbb S \arrow[d,"\mu_{(X \otimes \mathbb{S})\circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y \otimes \mathbb{S})}~(\varphi_{X \otimes \mathbb{S},Y \otimes \mathbb{S}} \otimes \mathbb{S})"] \\
   	((X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y\otimes \mathbb S)) \otimes \mathbb S \arrow[d,"\rho_{X \otimes \mathbb S ,Y \otimes \mathbb S}"]\\
    (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y\otimes \mathbb S)~.
   	\end{tikzcd}
   	\]
The universal property that defines the composition product $- \circ -$ allows us to change the second map $\mu_{(X \otimes \mathbb{S})\circ_\mathrm{pl} (Y \otimes \mathbb{S})} ~(\varphi_{X \otimes \mathbb{S},Y \otimes \mathbb{S}} \otimes \mathbb{S})$ by $(\mu_X \circ_\mathrm{pl} \mu_Y ) \otimes \mathbb{S}$ without modifying the whole composition. Then, the composition of the two first arrows is the identity, which implies that the whole composition is equal to its last component $\rho_{X \otimes \mathbb S ,Y \otimes \mathbb S}$, which concludes the proof.

label: prop: equal to the usual composition product
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{prop: equal to the usual composition product}
Let $M, N$ be two dg $\mathbb S$-modules. There is a natural isomorphism

\[
M \circ N(n) \cong \bigoplus_{k\geq 0} M(k) \otimes_{\mathbb{S}_k} \left( \bigoplus_{i_1 + \cdots + i_k = n} \mathrm{Ind}_{\mathbb{S}_{i_1} \times \cdots \times \mathbb{S}_{i_k}}^{\mathbb{S}_n} (N(i_1) \otimes \cdots \otimes N(i_k))\right)
\]
\vspace{0.1pc}

of dg $\mathbb S$-modules, where $\mathrm{Ind}$ stands for the induced representation.
head: environment
labels: prop: equal to the usual composition product

title: Proof
body_md: By Proposition \ref{lemmacompositioniso}, both expressions are isomorphic for free dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules. Furthermore, both expressions commute with sifted colimits. Hence both expressions are isomorphic for any pair of dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules.
head: environment

title: \sc Remark
body_md: Therefore Definition \ref{definitioncomp} coincides with the standard definition of the composition product of dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules present in the literature. See for instance \cite{LodayVallette}.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: The composition product $\circ$ defines the structure of a monoidal category on dg $\mathbb S$-module whose unit is given by $\mathcal{I}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X,Y,Z$ be three dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules. One can construct an associator isomorphism
\[
\begin{tikzcd}
\alpha_{X,Y,Z}: ((X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Y \otimes \mathbb S)) \circ (Z \otimes \mathbb S) 
\ar[r, "\cong"]
&(X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ ((Y \otimes \mathbb S) \circ (Z \otimes \mathbb S))~,
\end{tikzcd}
\]
using the binatural isomorphism $\psi$ of Proposition \ref{lemmacompositioniso} and the associator isomorphism of the composition product $\circ_\mathrm{pl}$ in the category of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules. Furthermore, this associator isomorphism commutes with the natural transformation $\mu: - \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S \longrightarrow - \otimes \mathbb S$, hence it induces an associator isomorphism for all free dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules. Using the compatibility of these constructions with sifted colimits, it induces a associator isomorphism for any three dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules. Likewise for the unitor isomorphisms. The commutativity of the required diagrams then follows from the commutativity of the unitors and the associators of the planar composition product $- \circ_\mathrm{pl} -$.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: The functor $-\otimes \mathbb S$ from dg $\mathbb N$-modules to dg $\mathbb S$-modules is strong monoidal.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: This structure of a strong monoidal functor is given by the identity map $\mathcal{I} \longrightarrow \mathcal{I} \otimes \mathbb S$ and the binatural map $\psi$ of Proposition \ref{lemmacompositioniso}. The fact that these maps define the structure of a strong monoidal functor is a direct consequence of the fact that they are used in the definition of the associator and the unitors related to the composition product.

title: Definition
body_md: A \textit{dg operad} $\mathcal{P}$ amounts to the data of a monoid $(\mathcal{P},\gamma,\eta)$ in the category of dg $\mathbb N$-modules with respect to the composition product.

body_md: The adjunction $- \otimes \mathbb S \dashv U_{\mathbb S}$ relating dg operads to planar dg operads is monadic since its right adjoint preserves coreflexive equalisers and is conservative. title: Definition
body_md:
The \textit{tree intertwining map} $\tau$ is the natural morphism of dg $\mathbb N$-modules
\[
\tau: \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(-\otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(-) \otimes \mathbb S) \otimes \mathbb S
\longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(-) \otimes \mathbb S.
\]
whose first part is given by the units of the monads $- \otimes \mathbb S$ and $\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}$ and whose second part is the monad product of $\mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(-) \otimes \mathbb S$.
head: environment
name: The tree intertwining map

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $g$ denote a full sub-groupoid of the groupoid of trees $\mathsf{Trees}$. Let us assume that $g$ is \textit{connected} within $\mathsf{Trees}$ in the sense that, for any isomorphism of trees $t \longrightarrow t'$, $t'$ belongs to $g$ whenever $t$ does. The \textit{planar endofunctor} $g_\mathrm{pl}(-)$ associated to $g$ is the endofunctor of dg $\mathbb N$-modules given, for a dg $\mathbb{N}$-module $X$, by
\[
g_\mathrm{pl}(X) \coloneqq \bigoplus_{t \in g} t(X)~,
\]
where the sum is taken over planar trees in $g$ up to planar isomorphisms.
head: environment
name: Planar endofunctor of a sub-groupoid

title: Proposition
body_md:
For every connected full sub-groupoid $g$ of $\mathsf{Trees}$, the tree intertwining map 
\[
\tau: \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (- \otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (-) \otimes \mathbb S
\]
restricts to a morphism
\[
\tau|_g: g_\mathrm{pl} (- \otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow g_\mathrm{pl} (-) \otimes \mathbb S.
\]
of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $X$ be a dg $\mathbb{N}$-module. It is suffices to prove that for every planar tree $t$, the map
\[
t(X \otimes \mathbb S) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (X \otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (X) \otimes \mathbb S
\]
factors through $g_\mathrm{pl} (-) \otimes \mathbb S$ where $g$ is the connected component of the groupoid of trees that contains $t$.
This can be done by induction on the height of trees. On the trivial tree, the tree intertwining map is given by the identity map of $\mathcal{I} \otimes \mathbb S$. On trees of height one, the tree intertwining map is given by the identity of $X \otimes \mathbb S$.

\medskip

Let us assume that it is satisfied for all tree of height equal or lower than $m$ for some natural integer $m \geq 1$. Let $t$ be a planar tree with $n$ leaves that is made up of a root node with $k \geq 1$ inputs and topped by $k$ subtrees $t_1, \ldots, t_k$ of height equal or lower than $m$ and with $n_1,\ldots, n_k$ leaves. The height of $t$ is thus lower or equal to $m+1$. Let us denote $g_i$ the connected component within the groupoid of tree of $t_i$ for $i \in \{1, \ldots, k\}$ and $g$ the connected component of $t$. On $t$, the intertwining map is the composition
$$
\begin{tikzcd}
t(X \otimes \mathbb S)(n) \coloneqq (X(k) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{k}]) \otimes t_1(X \otimes \mathbb S)(n_1)
 \otimes \cdots \otimes t_k(X \otimes \mathbb S)(n_k)
 \ar[d]
 \\
 (X(k) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{k}])
 \otimes (g_{1,\mathrm{pl}}(X)(n_1) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{n_1}])
 \otimes \cdots \otimes (g_{k,\mathrm{pl}}(X)(n_k) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{n_k}])
 \ar[d, "\cong"]
 \\
 \displaystyle \bigoplus_{t'_1 \in g_1} \cdots \bigoplus_{t'_k \in g_k}
 (X(k) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{k}])
 \otimes (t'_{1}(X)(n_1) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{n_1}])
 \otimes \cdots \otimes (t'_{k}(X)(n_k) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{n_k}])
 \ar[d,"\xi"]
 \\
  \displaystyle \bigoplus_{t'_1 \in g_1} \cdots \bigoplus_{t'_k \in g_k} \bigoplus_{\sigma \in \mathbb S_{k}}
 X(k) \otimes t'_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}(X)(n_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}) \otimes \cdots \otimes t'_{\sigma^{-1}(k)}(X)(n_{\sigma^{-1}(k)}) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{n}]
 \ar[d, "\cong"]
 \\
  \displaystyle \bigoplus_{t'_1 \in g_1} \cdots \bigoplus_{t'_k \in g_k} \bigoplus_{\sigma \in \mathbb S_{k}}
 \mathrm{graft}_k(t'_{\sigma^{-1}(1)} ,\ldots, t'_{\sigma^{-1}(k)}) (X)(n) \otimes \Bbbk[\mathbb S_{n}]
 \ar[d, hookrightarrow]
 \\
 \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (X) \otimes \mathbb S~.
\end{tikzcd}
$$
Here the third map $\xi$ is given by
\[
\xi: X(k) \otimes \sigma) 
 \otimes (t'_1(X) \otimes \sigma_{1})
 \otimes \cdots \otimes (t'_k(X) \otimes \sigma_k)
 \mapsto
 X(k) \otimes t'_{\sigma^{-1}(1)}(X) \otimes \cdots \otimes t'_{\sigma^{-1}(k)} \otimes \lambda~,
\]
where $\lambda \in \Bbbk[\mathbb S_n]$ is the composition $\sigma \circ (\sigma_1 \otimes \cdots \otimes \sigma_k)$
in the operad $u\mathcal{A} ss$. Moreover, for every planar trees $t'_1\in g_1, \ldots, t'_k \in g_k$, $\mathrm{graft}_k(t'_{\sigma^{-1}(1)} ,\ldots, t'_{\sigma^{-1}(k)})$ is the planar tree with a root node with $k$ inputs and toppped by the sub-trees, in order, $t'_1, \ldots, t'_k$. Therefore it is clear that it is isomorphic to $t$. Thus the map $t(X \otimes \mathbb S) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow  \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S$ factors through $g_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S$ and we can conclude by induction.

title: \sc Notation
body_md:
Let $n$ be a natural integer. For some particular sub-groupoids $g$, we use the following notations.

\medskip

\begin{itemize}
\item For $g$ being the sub-groupoid of non trivial trees, we denote $g(X)$ as $\overline{\mathbb{T}}(X)$, and call it the \textit{reduced tree} endofunctor.

\medskip

    \item For $g$ the sub-groupoid of trees of height at most $n$, we denote $g(X)$ as $\mathbb{T}_{\leq n}(X)$.
    
\medskip

    \item For $g$ the sub-groupoid of trees with $n$ nodes (resp. at most $n$ nodes), we denote $g(X)$ as $\mathbb{T}^{(n)}(X)$.
    
\medskip

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to notice that if $\overline{g}$ is the complement sub-groupoid of $g$ in $\mathsf{Trees}$, then the map
\[
\nu_X: \mathbb{T} (X \otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (X) \otimes \mathbb S
\]
rewrites as the sum

    \nu_X|_g \oplus \nu_X|_{\overline g} :
    g (X \otimes \mathbb S) \oplus \overline g (X \otimes \mathbb S)
    \longrightarrow g_\mathrm{pl} (X) \otimes \mathbb S \oplus \overline g_\mathrm{pl} (X) \otimes \mathbb S~.

Let $g$ be a connected full sub-groupoid of of the groupoid of trees $\mathsf{Trees}$. Let $M$ be a dg $\mathbb{S}$-module. The isomorphism

title: Proof
body_md:
It suffices to prove the result for $g$ the whole groupoid of trees $\mathsf{Trees}$. This amounts to prove that the following diagrams 
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \mathbb{T} (\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\mathbb{T}(\mu_{\mathbb{T}})"] \ar[d,"\nu_{\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S}",swap]

        \ar[d,"\nu_{\mathrm{U}(M)}"]

        \ar[r,"\tau_{\mathrm{U}(M)}"]
        & \mathbb{T}_\mathrm{pl} (\mathrm{U}(M)) \otimes \mathbb S

    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]

        \ar[r,"\nu_{\mathrm{U}(M)}"] \ar[rd,"\pi_M ",swap]

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemmaconilpotentcooperadlemmaone}
Let $X$ be a dg $\mathbb{N}$-module. The tree intertwining map $\tau$ is compatible with the planar cooperad structure of the reduced planar tree comonad. That is, the following diagram 
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[rr, "\tau_{X}"] \ar[d,"\Delta",swap]
        && \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S 
        \ar[d,"\Delta \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
        \\

        \ar[r,"\tau_{X} \circ_\mathrm{pl} \tau_{X}"]
        & (\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\varphi"]
        & (\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)  \circ_\mathrm{pl} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S,
    \end{tikzcd}
   	\]
commutes in the category of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules. Here $\Delta$ is the planar cooperad structure of $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S)$ the horizontal map $\varphi$ is the lax monoidal functor structure on $- \otimes \mathbb S$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let us prove this result by induction on the height of the trees. This amounts to show that for every natural integer $n \geq 1$, the pre-compositions by the inclusion $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}(X \otimes \mathbb S)$ of the arrows in the square diagram are equal.

\medskip

For trees of height $n=1$, the diagram above restricts to
    \[

        X \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r, "\mathrm{Id}"] \ar[d, "\cong"']
        & X \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[d, "\cong"]
        \\

        \ar[r]

    \]
    which commutes. Let us assume that the result is satisfied up to a natural integer $n \geq 1$. Now, let us consider the following diagram
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\Delta_{\leq n+1}"] \ar[d, "\cong"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1} (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d, "\cong"]
        \\
        (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl} ~ \Delta_{\leq n}"] \ar[dd,"\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl}~ (\tau_X)_{\leq n}",swap]
        & (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X\otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl}~ (\tau_X)_{\leq n} \circ_\mathrm{pl}~ (\tau_X)_{\leq n}"]
        \\
        & (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)\otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl}~ \varphi"]
        \\
        (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl} ~ \Delta_{\leq n}"] \ar[d,"\varphi",swap]
        & (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X))\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\varphi"]
        \\
        (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"(\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl} ~ \Delta_{\leq n})\otimes \mathbb{S}"] \ar[d, "\cong"']
        & (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[d, "\cong"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\Delta_{\leq n+1} \otimes \mathbb S"]
        & (\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S~,
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$
    where the top horizontal and the bottom horizontal isomorphisms are,respectively: 
    \[
    \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \cong (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X\otimes \mathbb S) \quad \text{and} \quad (X \circ_\mathrm{pl} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S \cong \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X) \otimes \mathbb S~,
    \]
    where the first one is given by Corollary \ref{corollary: iso de la récurrence sur les arbres}. One can check that both of these isomorphisms are compatible with the planar cooperad structures, hence the top and the bottom squares commute. The second cell square commutes by induction hypothesis and the third by naturality of $\varphi$. Combined with the fact that the two following square diagrams 
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\cong"] \ar[dd,"\tau_X",swap]
        & (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\mathrm{Id} ~\circ_\mathrm{pl} \tau_X"]
        \\
        & (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\varphi"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\cong"]
        & (X  \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X))\otimes \mathbb S~,
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=3.5pc]
        (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)\otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\varphi ~\circ_\mathrm{pl}~\mathrm{Id}"] \ar[d,"\mathrm{Id} ~\circ_\mathrm{pl}~\varphi",swap]
        & ((X \circ_\mathrm{pl}{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X))\otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\varphi"]
        \\
        (X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} (({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X))\otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\varphi"]
        & (X  \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X) \circ_\mathrm{pl}{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X))\otimes \mathbb S~,
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$
commute, it yields the result at level $n+1$.

label: lemmaconilpotentcooperadcomonad
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemmaconilpotentcooperadcomonad}
Let $X$ be a dg $\mathbb{N}$-module. The tree intertwining map $\tau$ is compatible with the comonad structure $\delta$ on the reduced tree comonad. That is, the following natural diagrams are commutative

    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[rr,"\tau_X"] \ar[d,"\delta_{X \otimes \mathbb{S}}"']
        && \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S 
        \ar[d,"\delta_{X} \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\tau_X)"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\tau_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)}"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S~.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\tau_X"] \ar[rd,"\eta_{~\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S)}"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S 
        \ar[d,"\eta_{~\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S}"]
        \\
        &X \otimes \mathbb S~.
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    
in the category of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The fact that the second diagram is commutative is clear. Let us prove that the first one is commutative.
As in the proof of Lemma \ref{lemmaconilpotentcooperadlemmaone}, we prove the result by an induction on the height of the trees. More precisely, it suffices to prove that the pre-compositions by the inclusion $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \hookrightarrow\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}}(X \otimes \mathbb S)$ of the arrows in the square diagram are equal. For $n=1$, this result is clear.

\medskip

Let us assume that it is satisfied for up to a natural integer $n \geq 1$. Then, it is satisfied for $n+1$ since the following diagram is commutative

    {\scriptsize{
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[rr,"(\tau_X)_{\leq n+1}"] \ar[d,"\Delta_{\leq n+1}",swap]
        && \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X) \otimes \mathbb S 
        \ar[d,"\Delta_{\leq n+1} \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"(\tau_X)_{\leq n+1}\circ_\mathrm{pl}(\tau_X)_{\leq n}"]
        \ar[d,"\mathrm{Id} ~ \circ_\mathrm{pl} ~ (\delta_{X \otimes \mathbb{S}})_{\leq n}",swap]
        &(\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X) \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X) \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\varphi"]\ar[d,"\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl} (\delta_{\leq n} \otimes \mathbb{S})"]
        & ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X)  \circ_\mathrm{pl} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[d,"(\mathrm{Id} \circ_\mathrm{pl} \delta_{\leq n}) \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"(\tau_X)_{\leq n+1}\circ_\mathrm{pl}(\tau)_{\leq n}",swap] \ar[d]
        & (\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X) \otimes \mathbb S) \circ_\mathrm{pl} ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X) \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\varphi"]
        & ({\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X)  \circ_\mathrm{pl} {\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[d]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[rr,"\tau_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X)}~\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}((\tau_X)_{\leq n+1})"]
        && (\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\mathrm{pl}, \leq n+1}(X)) \otimes \mathbb S~,
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$}}
    which is a consequence of Lemma \ref{lemmaconilpotentcooperadlemmaone} and of the induction hypothesis.
head: environment

label: lemmatreecomonad
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lemmatreecomonad}
Let $X$ be a dg $\mathbb{N}$-module. The monad structure $\mu$ of the functor $-\otimes \mathbb{S}$ is compatible with the comonad structure $\delta$ on the reduced tree comonad and the tree intertwining map $\tau$. That is, the following diagram is commutative
    \[
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}(X \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\nu_{X \otimes \mathbb{S}}"] \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mu_X)"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S )\otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\delta_{X \otimes \mathbb S}"] \ar[d,"\mu_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)}~(\tau_X \otimes \mathbb S)"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\nu^{-1})~ \nu^{-1}_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}"] \ar[d,"\mu_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}~\tau_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}~\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\tau)"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(X \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mu_X)"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}(X \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[r,"\nu_{X}"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)\otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\delta_X \otimes \mathbb{S}"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)\otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\nu^{-1})~ \nu^{-1}_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}"']
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(X \otimes \mathbb S).
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
    in the category of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The commutation of the left side square is a consequence of Proposition \ref{corollarytreemodcommutation}. The commutation of the middle square is a consequence of Lemma \ref{lemmaconilpotentcooperadcomonad}. The right square decomposes into the following diagram
    $$
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S )\otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\nu^{-1}_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}"] \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\tau)",swap]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X \otimes \mathbb S) \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\tau)"] \ar[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\nu^{-1})"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(X \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[dd,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mu_X)"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S )\otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\nu^{-1}_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}"] \ar[d,"\mu_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}~\tau_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}",swap]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S )
        \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mu_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}})"]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)\otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\nu^{-1}_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X) \otimes \mathbb S )
        \ar[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\nu^{-1})"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(X \otimes \mathbb S)~,
    \end{tikzcd}
    $$
    which is commutative. Indeed, its top left cell is clearly commutative, its bottom left cell is the left square in the lemma applied to $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(X)$, and its right cell is the image by $\overline{\mathbb{T}}(-)$ of the same left square in the lemma.
head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
The reduced tree endofunctor $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$ on the category of dg $\mathbb S$-module has the canonical structure of a comonad. For a dg $\mathbb{S}$-module $M$, 

\begin{enumerate}
\item its counit $\epsilon: \overline{\mathbb{T}}(M) \longrightarrow M$ is the canonical projection into the corollas,

\medskip

\item its coproduct $\delta_M: \overline{\mathbb{T}}(M) \longrightarrow \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(M)$ is the unique arrow which makes the following diagram 
 \[
    \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3.25pc,row sep=3.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}(M)
        \ar[rrr,"\delta_M"]
        &&&
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(M)
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb{S})
        \ar[u,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\pi_M)"] \ar[r,"\nu_{\mathrm{U}(M)}"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathrm{U}(M)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\delta_{\mathrm{U}(M)} \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
        &\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathrm{U}(M)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\nu^{-1})~ \nu^{-1}_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}"]
        &\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb{S}).
        \ar[u,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\pi_M)"']
    \end{tikzcd}
    \]
commute, where $\pi_M: \mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb{S} \longrightarrow M$ is the map given by the dg $\mathbb{S}$-module structure.
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The natural map 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb{S})
        \ar[r,"\nu_{\mathrm{U}(M)}"]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathrm{U}(M)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\delta_{\mathrm{U}(M)} \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
        &\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}(\mathrm{U}(M)) \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\nu^{-1})~ \nu^{-1}_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}}"]
        &\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb{S})
\end{tikzcd}
\]
induces a morphism of diagrams
\[
\left(\begin{tikzcd}
    \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\pi_M)", shift left=1.1ex] \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mu_{\mathrm{U}(M)})",swap,shift right=1.1ex]
    \\
    \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)
\end{tikzcd}\right)
\longrightarrow
\left(\begin{tikzcd}
    \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\pi_M)", shift left=1.1ex] \ar[d,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mu_{\mathrm{U}(M)})", swap, shift right=1.1ex]
    \\
    \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)
\end{tikzcd}\right)
\]
as a consequence of Lemma \ref{lemmatreecomonad}. Taking the colimits of these diagrams, one obtains a natural coproduct map
\[
\delta_M: \overline{\mathbb{T}}(M) \longrightarrow \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(M)~.
\]
It remains to show that this coproduct map and the counit endow the endofunctor $\overline{\mathbb{T}}(-)$ with a comonad structure.

\medskip

The counitality is straightforward to check. Let us prove that the coproduct map is coassociative. Since $\overline{\mathbb{T}}(-)$ preserves epimorphisms and since the map $\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S \longrightarrow M$ is an epimorphism, it suffices to prove that 
the following square diagram
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
    \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[r, "\delta_{\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S}"] \ar[d, "\delta_{\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S}"']
    & \overline{\mathbb{T}} \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[d, "\delta_{\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)}"]
    \\
    \overline{\mathbb{T}} \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)
    \ar[r, "\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\delta_{\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S})"']
    & \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)
\end{tikzcd}
\]
is commutative. This follows from the coassociativity of coproduct map $\delta_\mathrm{pl}: \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} \longrightarrow \overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$ and from the fact that the natural isomorphism
\[
\nu_{\mathrm{U}(M)}^{-1}: \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M))_\mathrm{pl} \otimes \mathbb S \longrightarrow \overline{\mathbb{T}}(\mathrm{U}(M) \otimes \mathbb S)
\]
is suitably compatible with the coproducts.
head: environment

title: \sc Remark
body_md:
One can notice that the natural isomorphism 
\[
\nu: \overline{\mathbb{T}}(- \otimes \mathbb S) \longrightarrow \overline{\mathbb{T}}(-)_\mathrm{pl} \otimes \mathbb S
\]
between functors from the category of dg $\mathbb{N}$-modules to the category of dg $\mathbb S$-modules is a comonad transformation above the functor $- \otimes \mathbb S$. More precisely, this amounts to the following diagrams commuting
\[
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}(-)_\mathrm{pl} \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r] \ar[d]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}(- \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d]
        \\
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(-)_\mathrm{pl} \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}\overline{\mathbb{T}}(- \otimes \mathbb S)
    \end{tikzcd}
    \quad 
    \begin{tikzcd}
        \overline{\mathbb{T}}(-)_\mathrm{pl} \otimes \mathbb S
        \ar[r] \ar[rd]
        & \overline{\mathbb{T}}(- \otimes \mathbb S)
        \ar[d]
        \\
        & - \otimes \mathbb S~.
    \end{tikzcd}
\]
This induces by (co)doctrinal adjunction the following corollary.

body_md:
\label{corollaryadjunctionconilp}
The adjunction 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3.5pc,row sep=0.5pc]
          \mathsf{dg}~\mathbb{N}\text{-}\mathsf{mod} \arrow[r, shift left=1.1ex, "- \otimes \mathbb S"{name=A}]

lifts canonically to an adjunction 
\[

          &\mathsf{dg}~\overline{\mathbb{T}}\text{-}\mathsf{cog} ~. \arrow[l, shift left=.75ex, "U_{\mathbb S}"{name=B}]
             \arrow[phantom, from=A, to=B, , "\dashv" rotate=90]

head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(X,\delta_X)$ be a dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebra. The dg $\mathbb{S}$-module inherits a dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$-coalgebra structure given by
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=0.5pc]
X \otimes \mathbb{S} \arrow[r,"\delta_X \otimes \mathbb{S}"]
&\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} (X)  \otimes \mathbb S \arrow[r,"\nu_X"]
&\overline{\mathbb{T}} (X \otimes \mathbb S)~.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
Let $(M,\delta_M)$ be a dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$-coalgebra. The dg $\mathbb{N}$-module $\mathrm{U}(M)$ inherits a dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl}$-coalgebra given by 
\[
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=0.5pc]
\mathrm{U}(M) \arrow[r,"\mathrm{U}(\delta_M)"]
&\mathrm{U}(\overline{\mathbb{T}}(M)) \arrow[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}(\eta_M)"]
&\mathrm{U}(\overline{\mathbb{T}} (\mathrm{U}(M)  \otimes \mathbb S)) \arrow[r,"\nu_{\mathrm{U}(M)}"]
&\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} (\mathrm{U}(M)) \otimes \mathbb S) \arrow[r,"\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} (\pi_M)"]
&\overline{\mathbb{T}}_\mathrm{pl} (\mathrm{U}(M))~.
\end{tikzcd}
\]
One can check that these two natural constructions produce adjoint functors.

        \ar[lll, "\cong",swap]

    \]
is a commutative diagram.

title: Corollary
body_md:
Let $n$ be a natural integer. 

\medskip

\begin{enumerate}
\item The comonad structure on the reduced tree endofunctor $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$ restricts to $\overline{\mathbb{T}}_{\leq n}$ and $\overline{\mathbb{T}}^{(\leq n)}$. 

\medskip

\item The adjunction 
\[

body_md:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a conilpotent dg cooperad. Its $n$-\textit{coradical filtration} is given by the conilpotent dg cooperad $\mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_n \mathcal{C}$. It induces a ladder diagram 
\[

\]
indexed by $\mathbb{N}$, where all the arrows are monomorphisms.

title: \sc Remark
body_md:
If the characteristic of the base field $\Bbbk$ is zero, both the tree module $\mathbb{T} (-)$ and the composition product $\circ$ preserve {\bf{finite}} cosifted limits. Therefore the forgetful functors from (conilpotent) dg cooperads to dg $\mathbb S$-modules preserve these limits. Moreover, as in the planar case, given a dg cooperad $\mathcal{C}$, the conilpotent dg cooperad $\overline{\mathrm{F}}_n \mathcal{C}$ fits in the following pullback diagram
\[
        \begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5pc,row sep=2.5pc]
           \mathrm{F}^{\mathrm{rad}}_n \mathcal{C} \arrow[dr, phantom, "\lrcorner", very near start]
            \ar[r] \ar[d]
            & \overline{\mathbb{T}}^{(\leq n)} \mathcal{C}
            \ar[d,rightarrowtail]
            \\
            \mathcal{C}
            \ar[r,"\delta_\mathcal{C}"]
            & \overline{\mathbb{T}} \mathcal{C}~,
        \end{tikzcd}
\]
in the category of dg $\mathbb{S}$-modules, where $\delta_\mathcal{C}$ denotes the dg $\overline{\mathbb{T}}$-coalgebra structure of $\mathcal{C}$.

title: Definition
body_md: Let $t$ be a planar tree. A \textit{node} (or \textit{vertex}) of $t$ is an edge $e$ that is not a leaf. The inputs of this nodes are the edges $e'$ that are strictly greater than $e$ so that there are no edge between $e$ and $e'$. Sometimes, the edge that defines the node is called the output edge of this node. Moreover, the number of inputs of a node is called its arity.

title: Definition
body_md:
Let $t,t'$ be two trees. An i\textit{isomorphism of trees} from $t$ to $t'$ is an isomorphism of posets from $(\mathrm{edges}(t), <)$ to $(\mathrm{edges}(t'), <)$ that restricts to a bijection between leaves; thus it restricts to a bijection between nodes.

\medskip

An \textit{isomorphism of planar trees} from $t$ to $t'$ is an isomorphism of trees that preserves also the planar order.

title: Definition

    is the groupoid whose objects are planar trees and whose
